protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; RULE-GOVERNED file-08 content change under D-001 MF-6
verdictBasis: The decision merits pass. Every attack axis in the dispatch fails, the six adoption claims are true, the arithmetic is complete, and the entry is conservative in exactly the place it would be easiest not to be. Both SHOULD-FIX findings are about the artifact's own completeness rather than its substance, and both are cheap to fix.

shouldFixRecorded.location: header line 3 — '> **Status:** DRAFT — not yet dispatched.'
shouldFixRecorded.finding: The subject asserts it has not been dispatched while it is the frozen subject of this turn-1 review, held at chmod 0444. It is false as read.
shouldFixRecorded.whyThisGrade: This is not a first occurrence. I raised the identical defect as C2-D051-053-SF1 on the D-051/052/053 turn-1 draft, the coordinator accepted it and repaired it at turn 2, and the correct form — 'DRAFT — under review' — is in active use across D-060, D-061, D-065, D-066 and D-068. A finding that was raised, accepted and repaired one family earlier, then reappears, is if anything a stronger candidate for the same grade rather than a weaker one. Grading it lower here would make the earlier repair look arbitrary.
shouldFixRecorded.whyNotMustFix: It touches no decision content, and the status line is replaced wholesale at adoption — every adopted entry I have sampled carries '**ADOPTED <date>.**' plus reviewer verdicts — so the false clause never reaches the register.

shouldFixRecorded.finding: The measured-inputs section is an unfilled placeholder. The subject pins no digest of any kind: I counted zero 64-hex tokens in the whole file. This is the one entry in the family whose operative act is to mutate the authoritative register, and it does not pin the pre-edit digest of the file it is about to edit. Every one of the five sibling entries I checked — D-060, D-061, D-065, D-066, D-068 — pins file 08 at 6547e6ac…, and none of them edits it.
concreteConsequences: The reversibility clause reads 'C-D067 plus restore of the prior file-08 cells', but 'the prior file-08 cells' are not pinned anywhere, so the overturn procedure names a restore target the entry never fixes. D-000 clause 3 lists the overturn procedure among the mandatory recorded elements.
Clause 1 bounds the edit to six named rows with lead labels preserved. Without a pre-image digest there is no baseline against which a later auditor can confirm the edit stayed inside that bound.
Clause 1 directs that each appended note name a 'disposition digest', so this entry authorizes writing specific digests into the authoritative register while stating none of them.
shouldFixRecorded.whyNotMustFix: The information is recoverable rather than absent. The six owner-recording entries are named explicitly, each pins its own disposition digest, and git preserves file 08's pre-edit state at the commit boundary, so the edit can be reconstructed and reversed with one hop of extra work. The entry is under-specified, not unspecified, and it asserts nothing false.
shouldFixRecorded.fix: Fill the section: file 08's pre-edit sha256, COORD's sha256, and the six disposition digests the notes will carry — matching the table form every sibling entry already uses.

summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. The substance is sound and in one respect notably careful: this is the entry that could most easily have over-claimed, and it does not. All six owner recordings it names are genuinely ADOPTED and correctly mapped to their rows, including D-068, which was adopted after I reviewed it. Lead labels are preserved rather than promoted, no new status token is introduced, and the four rows without owner recordings are held at their live labels — which is doubly right, because the DR-006/DR-007/DR-009 Route B selections went CONTESTED and are parked, so those rows lack even a settled route election. My objection is entirely about the artifact's completeness: it says it has not been dispatched while under review, and it pins not a single digest despite being the one entry that edits file 08.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: f75fe1e66fbec2cd1dcc7ef597297e7bea30abc080f4be33973343066ab9bda2, three measurements at start and again at end, equal to the dispatched frozen digest, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at cfa07460960def42c89d63c7f28a053c298b1dcf1b158bc25786506841ecf3d6, also read-only.

All six adoption claims are true and correctly attributed. D-058 (DR-002), D-065 (DR-003), D-064 (DR-004), D-060 (DR-005), D-061 (DR-008 integration half) and D-068 (DR-010) are each present in COORD, each ADOPTED, and each names its claimed row in its own title. I checked D-068 specifically because I reviewed it at turn 1 while it was still a draft; it has since been adopted, so 'now ADOPTED' is accurate rather than anticipatory.

The claim 'File 08 cells still lead HARD-BLOCKED (DR-008 PARTIALLY SATISFIED)' is true against live bytes. DR-002, DR-003, DR-004, DR-005 and DR-010 all lead HARD-BLOCKED; DR-008 leads 'PARTIALLY SATISFIED 2026-08-12 — posture half closed, integration half open'; and DR-001 leads SATISFIED, matching clause 2's 'DR-001 stays SATISFIED'.

The attack 'counts DR-006/007/009/011 as disposed' fails, and the entry is more conservative than it strictly had to be. Clause 2 holds those four 'stay as their live labels' — all four are HARD-BLOCKED — and clause 4 states condition 1 does not discharge until they 'also have SATISFIED or scoped owner-recorded dispositions'. I confirmed no owner recording exists for DR-006, DR-007 or DR-009: the only entries touching those rows are the D-051 / D-052 / D-053 Route B selections, and those are recorded '**CONTESTED** after three turns under D-000 clause 2. Not adopted. No forced consensus. Parked.' So those rows lack even an adopted route election, let alone a disposition, and treating them as undisposed is correct.

The condition-1 arithmetic is complete and non-overlapping. DR-001 through DR-011 is eleven rows; the six this entry notes, the four it holds back, and DR-001 partition that set exactly, with no row counted twice and none omitted.

The attack 'new file-08 status token' fails. Clause 1 states 'Lead labels stay **HARD-BLOCKED** (or **PARTIALLY SATISFIED** for DR-008 posture)' and 'Do not invent a new status token.' I enumerated the leading status tokens actually in use across file 08's DR rows — HARD-BLOCKED, SATISFIED, PARTIALLY, OPEN, ACCEPTED, SPECIFIED, PROPOSED, DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, BLOCKED, RELEASE-QUALIFICATION-ONLY and others — and the labels this entry preserves are all existing vocabulary.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails three ways: clause 3 states 'Does not mark any row SATISFIED', the readiness effect states 'Condition 1 remains NOT MET … Zero SATISFIED added', and the alternatives section rejects the promotion by name — 'Change lead labels to SATISFIED. Rejected: DR-204; D-054; owner recordings forbid it.'

The attacks 'freeze or claim-register motion' and 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' fail: clause 3 states 'Does not apply a V1 successor. Does not move the freeze or claim register. Does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/', and the header carries the same refusal.
Clause 2's edit target exists and is not invented: file 08 carries a heading '### Current position — measured snapshot, 2026-08-13', which is the dated snapshot the clause proposes to update.

The entry's premise that a cell note is a distinct reviewed act is consistent with the entries it follows. Each of D-060, D-061, D-065 and D-068 states 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6). A later cell note is a separate act', and this entry is that act, taken as its own D-000 cycle.

file 08 is currently unedited — it measures at the digest its siblings pin, and git reports zero modified tracked files — so this review is of the authorization, not of an already-performed edit. I wrote one file and edited and committed nothing.

objectNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and two SHOULD-FIX, and the shape matters: the decision merits pass. This entry had the most room in the family to over-claim — it is the one that touches the authoritative register — and it does not take any of it. Lead labels are preserved, no status token is invented, the promotion to SATISFIED is rejected by name, and the four rows without owner recordings are held back, which is doubly correct given their selections are CONTESTED and parked. What I cannot consent to is a register-mutating entry that pins no digest at all, including of the file it edits, leaving its own overturn procedure pointing at an unfixed restore target; and a status line that says the file has not been dispatched, which is the same finding I raised on D-051/052/053, which was accepted and repaired there. Both fixes are mechanical and neither disturbs the decision.
